adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Nephrotic-range glomerular protein loss causes acquired loss of anticoagulant proteins. Renal vein thrombosis is a classic venous complication; antithrombin is the specific endogenous inhibitor whose loss removes inhibition of thrombin/Xa.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Fibrinogen and factor VIII are procoagulant rather than anticoagulant proteins, and nephrotic hypercoagulability can involve several changes. The question asks which urinary plasma-protein loss most directly causes loss of endogenous anticoagulant activity; antithrombin uniquely fits.
